title: $4399 For a Chinese Frame! Incolor SSR Review | NERO Show x JOIN Cycling

takeaways.text: US$4,399 in May 2026 for frame, fork, integrated bar and seat-mast topper.

Very stiff, especially the front: the bayonet front end plus a heavy (over 400 g) 150 mm integrated bar gave Factor One-level front stiffness, a heavy, disjointed feel out of the saddle and harsh front-end comfort; rear comfort was normal for a race bike.
A tire measuring 34 mm left about 6 mm of hex-key room each side; he thought 38 mm would fit the frame but would approach the front derailleur on 2×.
Built without wheels, his Ultegra SSR weighed 4.82 kg against 4.62 kg for a SRAM Red Giant Propel; much of the gap is the heavy 150 mm bar.

The integrated seat mast came with no height spacers, so saddle height changes need spacers cut from the mast off-cut; the supplied aero bottles leaked badly and were unusable, though the 3D-printed titanium small parts impressed him.
Incolor's size 60 rides like a high-stack 58 (404 mm reach, 598 mm stack), about 11–16 mm taller than a Propel or Factor at the same reach, and the stock bar adds 2 cm rise.

On 32 mm tires at about 50 psi (measuring 34 mm) the comfort gap to the Propel mostly closed, but the heavy front remained; he suggests a lighter, more compliant aftermarket bar and would still pick the Propel for most riders.

disclosure: NERO Show podcast review after about three weeks of riding; the hosts cite feedback from the founder of Panda Podium, an Incolor retailer, and the episode carries unrelated sponsors. How the test bike was obtained is not stated.
summary: NERO Show road review of an Incolor SSR with Shimano Ultegra 2×, compared back-to-back with a Giant Propel Advanced SL; the rest of the episode covers the Shanghai bike show.
